questions.stem: A checkout form collects a discount code in a StringBuilder, and the service checks it with `Objects.equals(expected, typed)`, where `expected` is the String "WINTER10" and `typed` holds the same eight characters. What does the check return?

options.text: true, since Objects.equals compares the characters of its two arguments
options.says: Objects.equals only adds null-safety and then calls String.equals, which is true only for another String

options.text: true, since Objects.equals turns both arguments into Strings when their types differ
options.says: Objects.equals converts nothing; it calls the first argument's equals

options.text: false, since Objects.equals calls the String's equals, which accepts only another String
options.says: String.equals is true only when its argument is a String with the same units, and Objects.equals calls it

options.text: false, since Objects.equals compares the two references when their types differ
options.says: Objects.equals calls the first argument's equals whenever that argument is not null, whatever the second one's type

origin.section: equals Is True Only for Another String, and Its Receiver Must Not Be null

questions.stem: An upload service refuses a file whose name is already in a HashSet<String>. `Résumé.pdf` arrives first from a laptop that sends each é as e followed by U+0301, then from a phone that sends each é as U+00E9. What happens to the phone's upload?

options.text: It is refused, since names that render alike get the same hash code
options.says: the hash code is computed from the UTF-16 units, and the two names have different units

options.text: It is refused, since String.equals treats the two encodings of é as the same text
options.says: equals compares units exactly; canonically equivalent forms are equal only after normalizing

options.text: It is accepted, since the two names hold different code points and so are different Strings
options.says: the decomposed name is longer and has other units, so its hash code and equals both differ and the set keeps both

options.text: It is accepted, since a HashSet compares names by reference and the two are separate objects
options.says: a HashSet uses hashCode and equals; two separate objects with the same units would be found

origin.section: Text That Looks the Same Can Be Different Code Points: Normalize Before Comparing

questions.stem: A Sku class's equals returns `code.equalsIgnoreCase(other.code)` and its hashCode returns `code.hashCode()`. A HashMap<Sku, Integer> holds 7 for new Sku("ab-12"). What does `stock.get(new Sku("AB-12"))` return?

options.text: 7, since the map asks equals, and equals ignores the difference in case
options.says: the map asks equals only about keys with the same hash code, and the two codes hash differently

options.text: 7, since the map tries equals on every key when no hash code matches
options.says: a hash map looks only in the bucket the hash code picks; it never scans every key

options.text: null, since the map looks for a key with the same hash code before it asks equals
options.says: "ab-12" and "AB-12" have different hash codes, so equals is never asked and the lookup finds nothing

options.text: null, since equalsIgnoreCase treats the digits and the dash as different in each case
options.says: equalsIgnoreCase returns true for the two codes; the lookup fails before it is called

origin.section: equalsIgnoreCase Has No Matching hashCode: Compare and Hash One Key

questions.stem: An invoice screen keeps customer names in `new TreeSet<>(collator)`, where the collator is for Locale.FRENCH with its strength set to PRIMARY. The names "Leila", "Léila" and "LEILA" are added. What does size() return?

options.text: 1, since the set keeps only one of the names its comparator calls equal
options.says: a TreeSet treats a comparator result of 0 as the same element, and at PRIMARY strength case and accents don't count

options.text: 1, since PRIMARY strength rewrites each name to its base letters as it is added
options.says: a collator changes no string; the set kept "Leila" as it was added and dropped the others

options.text: 3, since the set asks equals before it drops a name its comparator calls equal
options.says: a TreeSet never calls equals; the comparator alone decides what is a duplicate

options.text: 3, since PRIMARY strength changes only the order and never what counts as a duplicate
options.says: a TreeSet's duplicates are whatever its comparator returns 0 for, so a strength that ignores case and accents makes the three names one

origin.section: compareTo Orders UTF-16 Units; People Need a Collator, and Its 0 Merges Set Entries
